title: Power BI Workflow & Power Query Unpivoting (M Language)
summary: Understand the ETL boundary before VertiPaq compression and convert wide human-readable crosstab reports into machine-ready analytical rows.
learningObjectives: Separate Power Query upstream data shaping (M) from live DAX visual calculations
Reshape wide month columns cleanly via 'Unpivot Other Columns' maintaining long-term refresh compatibility

sections.heading: 1. Wide Crosstabs vs Long Relational Fact Tables
sections.content:
Analysts regularly inherit human-formatted Excel tabs sporting columns named `Jan-2026`, `Feb-2026`, ..., `Dec-2026`. If loaded as-is into Power BI, writing dynamic Year-over-Year filters becomes impossible cleanly—and next January breaks visuals when a new column appears!

Inside **Power Query**, selecting immutable anchor columns (`Product`, `Region`) and running **Unpivot Other Columns** collapses all month headers into two clean vertical columns (`Attribute: Month`, `Value: Sales`). Now a single `SUM(Sales[Value])` measure dynamically slices across every past and future month effortlessly!

codeExamples.code:
[Dirty Excel Crosstab]                   [Clean Star-Ready Fact Rows]
Region | Jan  | Feb     --(Unpivot)-->   Region | Month | Amount
North  | 100  | 120                      North  | Jan   | 100
                                         North  | Feb   | 120
codeExamples.explanation: Unpivoting transforms column headers into clean sliceable category rows automatically across future reloads.

keyPoints: Do all structural cleaning, splitting, trimming, and unpivoting in Power Query—NEVER load dirty wide spreadsheets into DAX!
Always set explicit data types (Currency/Decimal, Integer, Date) early.
commonMistakes: Selecting fixed month columns inside `Unpivot Columns` instead of `Unpivot Other Columns` (so next month's newly added column won't unpivot!).

sections.heading: 2. Foldable Power Query M Pipeline
sections.content: Notice how clean sequential M transformations filter out blank sub-totals cleanly and enforce strict locale types before compressing into the Power BI model.

codeExamples.code:
let
  Source = Excel.Workbook(File.Contents("C:\Data\RegionalSales.xlsx"), null, true),
  Sheet = Source{[Item="SalesData", Kind="Sheet"]}[Data],
  PromotedHeaders = Table.PromoteHeaders(Sheet, [PromoteAllScalars=true]),
  FilteredTotals = Table.SelectRows(PromotedHeaders, each [Region] <> "Grand Total" and [Region] <> null),
  UnpivotedMonths = Table.UnpivotOtherColumns(FilteredTotals, {"Region", "Category"}, "MonthLabel", "Revenue"),
  TypedTable = Table.TransformColumnTypes(UnpivotedMonths, {{"Revenue", Currency.Type}, {"Region", type text}})
in
  TypedTable
codeExamples.explanation: Removing Excel `Grand Total` footer rows in Power Query avoids double-counting sums 2x inside dashboards!
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Clean 4-column table ready for Star Schema relationship linking

keyPoints: Always remove embedded 'Subtotal' / 'Grand Total' spreadsheet summary rows early in Power Query.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to filter out Excel Total rows, causing every dashboard card to report double the genuine revenue!

exercises.objective: Eliminate double-counting totals and wide column layouts cleanly.
exercises.description: Your finance CSV exports quarterly totals (`Q1_Total` rows mixed inside raw data) and splits Revenue across 12 monthly columns (`2026-01` .. `2026-12`). State the exact Power Query steps in safe execution order.
instructions: Identify the step that prevents `Q1_Total` summary rows from doubling actual sums.
Specify how to reshape the 12 month headers cleanly without breaking when `2027-01` arrives.
Identify correct data types for numeric amounts vs string keys.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why should you use 'Unpivot Other Columns' anchored on fixed ID/Name columns rather than selecting Jan..Dec manually?

options.text: New future month columns added to source spreadsheets automatically unpivot cleanly during scheduled refreshes without editing M code
DAX cannot display dates unless stored as columns

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Anchoring fixed columns ensures schema resilience as new periods arrive.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What serious reporting error occurs if an Excel 'Grand Total' row stays inside a Power BI Fact table?

options.text: Power BI `SUM()` metrics aggregate BOTH line items AND the Grand Total row, silently doubling reported company revenue

knowledgeChecks.explanation: DAX aggregates every row dynamically—so Excel subtotal rows must ALWAYS be excluded upstream in Power Query.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: When transforming data from an external SQL database in Power Query, why monitor 'View Native Query' (Query Folding)?

options.text: It confirms filtering and joins push directly down to the fast source SQL database rather than pulling huge unindexed tables into Power BI RAM
It turns Excel tables into encrypted PDFs
It prevents calculated measures from updating on slicers

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Preserving query folding accelerates scheduled refreshes drastically.

recap: You distinguished upstream Power Query ETL cleanly and protected reports from Excel subtotal double-counting and wide schema fragility.
